$comment: Seeds the `exercises` table. muscleGroups/primaryMuscle use ids from reference/muscle-groups.json; equipment from reference/equipment.json; category and movementPattern from reference/exercise-categories.json. `met` is the Compendium of Physical Activities value and drives calorie-burn estimates. `regressions`/`progressions` reference ids within this file, forming beginner-to-advanced chains for each major pattern.

items.name: Bodyweight squat
items.description: The entry point to every squat pattern, teaching depth and knee tracking before load is added.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned slightly out.
Push the hips back and bend the knees, keeping the chest tall.
Descend until the thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Drive through the whole foot to stand.
formCues: Spread the floor with your feet
Keep the ribcage stacked over the pelvis
commonMistakes: Heels lifting off the floor
Rounding the lower back at the bottom

items.name: Goblet squat
items.description: A front-loaded squat that self-corrects posture, making it the best bridge to barbell work.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell vertically against the chest.
Squat down keeping the elbows inside the knees.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then stand.
formCues: Keep the weight glued to your sternum
Elbows point down, not out
commonMistakes: Letting the load drift away from the body
Cutting depth short

items.name: Barbell back squat
items.description: The primary lower-body strength builder and the anchor of most leg sessions.
instructions: Set the bar across the upper traps and unrack with braced trunk.
Take two steps back and set the feet shoulder-width.
Squat to at least parallel, keeping the bar over mid-foot.
Drive up without letting the hips shoot back first.
formCues: Big breath and brace before each rep
Push the floor away
commonMistakes: Knees caving inward
Hips rising faster than the chest
safetyNotes: Set safety pins at depth when training near failure
Never train to failure without a spotter or pins

items.name: Barbell front squat
items.description: Shifts load to the quads and demands far more trunk and upper-back control than the back squat.
instructions: Rack the bar on the front delts with elbows high.
Unrack, step back and brace hard.
Squat down keeping the torso as upright as possible.
Stand without letting the elbows drop.
formCues: Elbows up throughout
Stay tall through the chest
commonMistakes: Elbows dropping and the bar rolling forward
Losing the upper-back brace
safetyNotes: Practise dumping the bar forward safely before loading heavy

items.name: Smith machine squat
items.description: A fixed-path squat useful for beginners or for training close to failure without a spotter.
instructions: Set the bar at upper-trap height and position the feet slightly forward.
Unlock the bar and squat to depth.
Drive up and relock at the top.
formCues: Let the machine guide the path, not your posture
commonMistakes: Feet placed too far forward, straining the knees

items.name: Leg press
items.description: Loads the quads heavily with minimal trunk demand, useful when the lower back needs a break.
instructions: Sit with the back flat against the pad and feet mid-platform.
Lower until the knees reach roughly 90 degrees.
Press back without locking the knees hard.
formCues: Keep the lower back in contact with the pad
commonMistakes: Letting the pelvis tuck at the bottom
Slamming into full lockout
safetyNotes: Engage the safety catches before stepping out

items.name: Pistol squat
items.description: A single-leg squat to full depth demanding strength, balance and ankle mobility together.
instructions: Stand on one leg with the other extended forward.
Sit back and down under control to full depth.
Drive through the heel to stand without touching down.
formCues: Reach the arms forward as a counterbalance
commonMistakes: Collapsing at the bottom
Knee caving inward
safetyNotes: Build up with a box or counterweight before the full range

items.name: Glute bridge
items.description: Teaches hip extension without spinal load, the first step in any posterior-chain progression.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Press through the heels and lift the hips until the body forms a straight line.
Squeeze the glutes at the top, then lower under control.
formCues: Tuck the ribs down before lifting
Finish with the glutes, not the lower back
commonMistakes: Over-arching the lower back at the top

items.name: Barbell hip thrust
items.description: The highest-tension glute exercise available, loaded through a full range at the top.
instructions: Sit with the upper back against a bench and the bar over the hips.
Drive through the heels to lift the hips to full extension.
Pause at the top, then lower under control.
formCues: Chin tucked, ribs down
Finish hips level, not hyperextended
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back to fake range
Pushing through the toes
safetyNotes: Use a bar pad to protect the hips

items.name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
items.description: Teaches the hinge with a light, forgiving load before the barbell version.
instructions: Hold dumbbells in front of the thighs with soft knees.
Push the hips back, sliding the weights down the legs.
Stop when you feel a strong hamstring stretch, then stand.
formCues: Hips travel back, not down
Keep the weights close to the legs
commonMistakes: Turning it into a squat
Rounding the upper back

items.name: Romanian deadlift
items.description: Builds hamstring and glute strength through a loaded stretch without a floor reset.
instructions: Stand holding the bar at hip height with a braced trunk.
Hinge at the hips, keeping the bar in contact with the legs.
Lower to mid-shin or the end of your hamstring range, then stand.
formCues: Lats on, bar dragging the thighs
Neutral spine from head to pelvis
commonMistakes: Letting the bar drift forward
Bending the knees to reach lower
safetyNotes: Stop the descent when the back would round, not at a fixed height

items.name: Barbell deadlift
items.description: The heaviest full-body pull available and the benchmark posterior-chain lift.
instructions: Set the bar over mid-foot and grip just outside the knees.
Drop the hips, lift the chest and take the slack out of the bar.
Push the floor away and stand tall, locking the hips.
Return the bar by hinging back, not squatting down.
formCues: Take the slack out before you pull
Finish with glutes, not a lean-back
commonMistakes: Jerking the bar off the floor
Hips shooting up first
safetyNotes: Stop the set when spinal position degrades, not when reps run out

items.name: Kettlebell swing
items.description: A ballistic hinge that builds hip power and conditioning at the same time.
instructions: Hike the kettlebell back between the legs.
Snap the hips forward to float the bell to chest height.
Let it fall and absorb it with another hinge.
formCues: The arms are ropes, the hips are the engine
Stand tall and squeeze at the top
commonMistakes: Lifting the bell with the arms
Squatting instead of hinging
safetyNotes: Clear the space behind and in front before starting

items.name: Back extension
items.description: Strengthens the spinal erectors and glutes directly, useful for lower-back resilience.
instructions: Set the hips on the pad with the feet anchored.
Hinge down under control.
Extend back to a straight line, no further.
formCues: Stop at neutral, do not arch past it
commonMistakes: Hyperextending at the top
Swinging through reps

items.name: Machine leg curl
items.description: Isolates knee flexion, the half of hamstring function that hinges do not train.
instructions: Set the pad just above the heels.
Curl the heels toward the glutes.
Lower slowly under control.
formCues: Keep the hips pinned to the pad
commonMistakes: Lifting the hips to gain range

items.name: Nordic hamstring curl
items.description: A brutally hard eccentric knee-flexion exercise with strong evidence for hamstring injury reduction.
instructions: Kneel with the ankles anchored securely.
Lower the torso forward as slowly as possible, staying rigid.
Catch with the hands and push back to the start.
formCues: Hips stay extended, body in one line
commonMistakes: Hinging at the hips to cheat the range
safetyNotes: Always be ready to catch yourself with the hands
Expect severe soreness after the first sessions

items.name: Single-leg Romanian deadlift
items.description: Trains the hinge, balance and hip stability on one leg at a time.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in the opposite hand to the standing leg.
Hinge forward, letting the free leg extend behind as a counterbalance.
Return to standing under control.
formCues: Keep the hips square to the floor
commonMistakes: Opening the hip of the trailing leg
Rushing and losing balance

items.name: Wall push-up
items.description: The lowest-load pressing variation, appropriate for true beginners or return from injury.
instructions: Stand arm's length from a wall with hands at chest height.
Lower the chest toward the wall keeping the body straight.
Press back to the start.
formCues: Body in one line from head to heels
commonMistakes: Letting the hips sag or pike

items.name: Incline push-up
items.description: Reduces the load of a push-up by raising the hands, the natural step before the floor version.
instructions: Place the hands on a bench or box, slightly wider than the shoulders.
Lower the chest to the surface with the body rigid.
Press back up.
formCues: Squeeze the glutes to stop the hips sagging
commonMistakes: Flaring the elbows to ninety degrees

items.name: Push-up
items.description: The standard bodyweight press, trainable anywhere and scalable in both directions.
instructions: Set the hands under the shoulders with the body in a plank.
Lower until the chest is just off the floor, elbows at about 45 degrees.
Press back to full lockout.
formCues: Brace the trunk like a moving plank
Push the floor away at the top
commonMistakes: Hips sagging
Head poking forward to fake depth

items.name: Decline push-up
items.description: Raising the feet shifts load onto the upper chest and shoulders and increases difficulty.
instructions: Place the feet on a bench with the hands on the floor.
Lower the chest under control.
Press back up without letting the hips drop.
formCues: Keep the ribs down as the load shifts forward
commonMistakes: Losing the trunk brace as the incline increases

items.name: Archer push-up
items.description: Loads one arm at a time, the practical route toward a one-arm push-up.
instructions: Set up wider than a normal push-up.
Lower toward one hand, keeping the other arm straight.
Press back and alternate sides.
formCues: Keep the hips square as you shift
commonMistakes: Rotating the torso to reduce the load

items.name: Dumbbell bench press
items.description: Allows a natural pressing path and a deeper stretch than the barbell, with easier bailouts.
instructions: Lie back with the dumbbells at chest level.
Press up until the arms are extended over the chest.
Lower under control to a comfortable stretch.
formCues: Keep the shoulder blades pinned back and down
commonMistakes: Pressing the dumbbells together at the top
Bouncing out of the bottom
safetyNotes: Learn to set the dumbbells down safely from the bottom

items.name: Barbell bench press
items.description: The main upper-body pressing strength lift and the standard benchmark for pushing power.
instructions: Set the eyes under the bar and pin the shoulder blades back.
Unrack and bring the bar over the lower chest.
Lower to touch the chest, then press to lockout.
formCues: Drive the feet into the floor
Bend the bar apart as you press
commonMistakes: Elbows flared to ninety degrees
Bouncing the bar off the chest
safetyNotes: Use a spotter or safety arms
Never bench with collarless plates on a sloped bar

items.name: Cable chest fly
items.description: Isolates the chest with constant tension through a long adduction range.
instructions: Set the pulleys at chest height and take a staggered stance.
Bring the handles together in front of the chest with soft elbows.
Return under control to a stretch.
formCues: Think of hugging a barrel
Fixed elbow angle throughout
commonMistakes: Turning it into a press by bending the elbows

items.name: Parallel bar dip
items.description: A heavy bodyweight press for the lower chest and triceps with a large range of motion.
instructions: Support yourself on the bars with the arms locked.
Lower until the upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor.
Press back to lockout.
formCues: Lean forward slightly for chest, stay upright for triceps
commonMistakes: Dropping too deep and stressing the shoulder
Shrugging at the bottom
safetyNotes: Stop the descent at the point of shoulder discomfort

items.name: Ring dip
items.description: An unstable dip that adds significant shoulder and trunk stabilisation demand.
instructions: Support on the rings with them turned out at the top.
Lower under control keeping the rings close to the body.
Press back up and turn the rings out again.
formCues: Keep the rings pressed against the ribs
commonMistakes: Letting the rings drift wide
safetyNotes: Master parallel bar dips before attempting rings

items.name: Pike push-up
items.description: A bodyweight vertical press that builds toward the handstand push-up.
instructions: From a push-up position walk the feet in and pike the hips high.
Lower the crown of the head toward the floor.
Press back up to the piked start.
formCues: Keep the hips stacked over the shoulders
commonMistakes: Flattening into a normal push-up

items.name: Handstand push-up
items.description: The hardest bodyweight vertical press, requiring full overhead strength and balance.
instructions: Kick up to a handstand against a wall.
Lower the head toward the floor under control.
Press back to full lockout.
formCues: Ribs down, body in one line
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back to compensate
safetyNotes: Learn to bail sideways safely before training this

items.name: Dumbbell shoulder press
items.description: Builds overhead pressing strength with independent arms and a friendly joint path.
instructions: Start with the dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward.
Press overhead until the arms lock out.
Lower under control to the start.
formCues: Squeeze the glutes to stop the ribs flaring
commonMistakes: Leaning back into an incline press

items.name: Barbell overhead press
items.description: The primary standing vertical press, demanding full-body tension to stay rigid.
instructions: Take the bar at shoulder height with the elbows just in front.
Brace, then press the bar in a straight line past the face.
Lock out with the bar over mid-foot, then lower.
formCues: Move the head back, not the bar forward
Shrug up at lockout
commonMistakes: Excessive lower-back arch
Pressing around the face instead of past it
safetyNotes: Press inside a rack when working heavy

items.name: Dumbbell lateral raise
items.description: Isolates the side delts, which compound pressing alone does not fully develop.
instructions: Stand with light dumbbells at the sides, slight elbow bend.
Raise the arms out to shoulder height.
Lower slowly under control.
formCues: Lead with the elbows, not the hands
commonMistakes: Swinging with the hips
Going far above shoulder height

items.name: Lat pulldown
items.description: A scalable vertical pull that builds the strength needed for pull-ups.
instructions: Secure the thighs under the pads and grip wider than the shoulders.
Pull the bar to the upper chest, driving the elbows down.
Return under control to a full stretch.
formCues: Chest up, pull the elbows into your back pockets
commonMistakes: Leaning far back and turning it into a row
Pulling behind the neck

items.name: Band-assisted pull-up
items.description: Removes part of bodyweight so the full pull-up pattern can be trained with real range.
instructions: Loop a band over the bar and place a foot or knee in it.
Hang at full stretch, then pull the chin over the bar.
Lower under control to a straight-arm hang.
formCues: Start each rep from a dead hang
commonMistakes: Using a band so strong it removes all effort
safetyNotes: Check the band for wear before loading it

items.name: Pull-up
items.description: The benchmark upper-body pull, building the lats and the whole grip-to-back chain.
instructions: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip, shoulders active.
Pull until the chin clears the bar.
Lower under control to a full hang.
formCues: Pull the bar to you, not just yourself to it
Keep the ribs down
commonMistakes: Kipping unintentionally
Cutting the bottom range short

items.name: Weighted pull-up
items.description: Adds external load once bodyweight pull-ups are comfortable for sets of eight or more.
instructions: Attach load with a dip belt or hold a dumbbell between the feet.
Perform a strict pull-up through full range.
Lower under control.
formCues: Do not let added load shorten the range
commonMistakes: Adding weight before strict form is solid
safetyNotes: Ensure the load cannot slip free mid-set

items.name: Cable face pull
items.description: Trains the rear delts and upper back, balancing heavy pressing volume.
instructions: Set a rope at upper-chest height.
Pull toward the face, separating the hands as you go.
Return under control.
formCues: Lead with the elbows high and wide
commonMistakes: Using too much weight and rowing instead

items.name: Inverted row
items.description: A scalable bodyweight horizontal pull; raising or lowering the bar changes difficulty instantly.
instructions: Set a bar at hip height and hang underneath it.
Keep the body rigid and pull the chest to the bar.
Lower under control to straight arms.
formCues: Squeeze the glutes, body in one line
commonMistakes: Hips sagging
Shrugging instead of retracting

items.name: Suspension trainer row
items.description: An easily adjusted horizontal pull; changing foot position scales the load continuously.
instructions: Hold the handles and walk the feet forward to lean back.
Pull the chest to the hands, elbows close to the ribs.
Lower under control.
formCues: Stay rigid from head to heels
commonMistakes: Piking at the hips as fatigue sets in
safetyNotes: Check the anchor point before each session

items.name: Barbell bent-over row
items.description: The heaviest horizontal pull, building thickness across the whole upper back.
instructions: Hinge forward to roughly 45 degrees with a braced trunk.
Row the bar to the lower ribs.
Lower under control without losing the torso angle.
formCues: Torso angle stays fixed for the whole set
commonMistakes: Standing up as the set gets hard
Jerking the bar with the hips
safetyNotes: Stop if the lower back rounds

items.name: Single-arm dumbbell row
items.description: A supported unilateral row that lets each side be trained through a long range.
instructions: Brace one hand and knee on a bench with a flat back.
Row the dumbbell to the hip, elbow close to the body.
Lower to a full stretch.
formCues: Keep the shoulders level, do not twist
commonMistakes: Rotating the torso to lift more weight

items.name: Seated cable row
items.description: Constant-tension horizontal pull that is easy to load progressively and safe on the lower back.
instructions: Sit tall with a slight knee bend and grip the handle.
Pull to the lower ribs, squeezing the shoulder blades.
Return to a controlled stretch.
formCues: Chest proud, minimal torso swing
commonMistakes: Rocking back and forth to move the stack

items.name: Reverse lunge
items.description: The most knee-friendly lunge variation and the standard starting point for single-leg work.
instructions: Step one foot back and lower the rear knee toward the floor.
Keep the front shin close to vertical.
Drive through the front foot to return.
formCues: Most of the weight stays on the front leg
commonMistakes: Front knee travelling far past the toes
Torso collapsing forward

items.name: Walking lunge
items.description: Adds a dynamic, loaded component to the lunge and challenges balance between steps.
instructions: Hold dumbbells at the sides and step forward into a lunge.
Lower the back knee toward the floor.
Drive through the front foot and step straight into the next rep.
formCues: Stay tall, step long enough to keep the shin vertical
commonMistakes: Short steps that push the knee forward
Rushing and losing balance

items.name: Bulgarian split squat
items.description: A rear-foot-elevated split squat that loads one leg hard with modest external weight.
instructions: Place the rear foot on a bench and step the front foot forward.
Lower until the front thigh is about parallel.
Drive through the front foot to stand.
formCues: Set the stance long enough that the front knee stays stacked
commonMistakes: Stance too short, overloading the front knee
Pushing off the back foot

items.name: Dumbbell step-up
items.description: A single-leg push with a concentric emphasis, easy to scale by box height.
instructions: Place one foot fully on a box at about knee height.
Drive through that foot to stand tall on the box.
Lower under control without pushing off the floor.
formCues: Do not push off the trailing leg
commonMistakes: Bouncing off the bottom foot
Box set too high for control
safetyNotes: Use a stable surface that will not tip

items.name: Lateral lunge
items.description: Trains the frontal plane and the adductors, which forward-only training neglects.
instructions: Step wide to one side, keeping both feet facing forward.
Sit back into the stepping hip while the other leg stays straight.
Push back to the centre.
formCues: Hinge the hip of the bent leg back
commonMistakes: Letting the trailing foot roll
Turning it into a rotation

items.name: Farmer's walk
items.description: Builds grip, trap and trunk endurance under heavy load with almost no technique barrier.
instructions: Pick up a heavy weight in each hand with a flat back.
Stand tall and walk with controlled steps.
Set the weights down under control.
formCues: Shoulders back and down, do not let them round forward
commonMistakes: Leaning back
Dropping the weights from height
safetyNotes: Clear the walking path first

items.name: Suitcase carry
items.description: A one-sided carry that forces the obliques to resist side bending the whole way.
instructions: Hold a single heavy weight in one hand.
Walk tall, resisting the pull to one side.
Switch hands and repeat for the same distance.
formCues: Stay perfectly upright, shoulders level
commonMistakes: Leaning away from the load

items.name: Pallof press
items.description: The core anti-rotation exercise, training the trunk to resist twisting rather than create it.
instructions: Stand side-on to a cable set at chest height and hold the handle at the sternum.
Press the handle straight out, resisting the pull to rotate.
Return to the chest under control.
formCues: Squeeze the glutes and stay square to the front
commonMistakes: Letting the torso rotate toward the machine

items.name: Cable wood chop
items.description: Trains rotational power through the hips and trunk in a diagonal pattern.
instructions: Set the cable high and stand side-on with straight arms.
Rotate through the hips and pull down across the body.
Return under control without letting the weight pull you back.
formCues: Turn from the hips, not just the arms
commonMistakes: Rotating only at the lower back

items.name: Russian twist
items.description: A seated rotational core exercise that is simple to load and easy to program anywhere.
instructions: Sit with the knees bent and lean back to about 45 degrees.
Rotate the ball from hip to hip under control.
Keep the chest tall throughout.
formCues: Move the ribcage, not just the arms
commonMistakes: Rounding the back and swinging fast

items.name: Front plank
items.description: The baseline anti-extension hold, teaching the trunk to stay rigid under load.
instructions: Set the elbows under the shoulders and the body in one line.
Squeeze the glutes and tuck the ribs down.
Hold, breathing normally.
formCues: Push the floor away and round the upper back slightly
commonMistakes: Hips sagging
Holding the breath

items.name: Side plank
items.description: A lateral hold that trains the obliques and hip stabilisers to resist side bending.
instructions: Lie on one side with the elbow under the shoulder.
Lift the hips so the body forms a straight line.
Hold, then switch sides.
formCues: Stack the hips and shoulders
commonMistakes: Hips dropping
Rotating toward the floor

items.name: Dead bug
items.description: Trains trunk control against moving limbs with almost no spinal load.
instructions: Lie on your back with arms up and knees over the hips.
Press the lower back gently into the floor.
Extend the opposite arm and leg, then return and switch.
formCues: Keep the lower back flat the entire time
commonMistakes: Lower back arching as the limbs extend

items.name: Hollow body hold
items.description: A gymnastics staple that builds the rigid midline position used in most bodyweight skills.
instructions: Lie on your back and press the lower back into the floor.
Lift the shoulders and legs to form a shallow banana shape.
Hold while breathing steadily.
formCues: Lower back stays glued down; raise the limbs if it lifts
commonMistakes: Letting the lower back arch to go lower

items.name: Hanging knee raise
items.description: Trains the lower abs and hip flexors while adding grip and shoulder hang time.
instructions: Hang from a bar with active shoulders.
Raise the knees toward the chest, curling the pelvis up.
Lower under control without swinging.
formCues: Finish the rep by tilting the pelvis, not just lifting the thighs
commonMistakes: Swinging between reps
Only moving at the hip

items.name: Hanging leg raise
items.description: The straight-leg progression, substantially harder through the whole range.
instructions: Hang with the legs straight and shoulders active.
Raise the legs to at least hip height, curling the pelvis.
Lower slowly without swinging.
formCues: Control the lowering; that is where the work is
commonMistakes: Using momentum from the previous rep

items.name: Ab wheel rollout
items.description: The hardest common anti-extension exercise, loading the trunk through a long lever.
instructions: Kneel holding the wheel under the shoulders.
Roll forward as far as you can without the hips dropping.
Pull back to the start using the trunk and lats.
formCues: Tuck the ribs and keep a slight rounding of the back
commonMistakes: Lower back arching at full extension
Rolling further than the trunk can control
safetyNotes: Extend the range gradually; this exercise commonly aggravates the lower back if rushed

items.name: Mountain climber
items.description: A fast-paced plank variation that doubles as core work and conditioning.
instructions: Start in a push-up position with a braced trunk.
Drive one knee toward the chest, then switch quickly.
Keep the hips low throughout.
formCues: Hips stay level; do not bounce them up
commonMistakes: Hips rising with speed
Hands creeping forward

items.name: Dumbbell biceps curl
items.description: Direct elbow-flexion work that pulling compounds alone will not maximise.
instructions: Stand with dumbbells at the sides, palms forward.
Curl the weights to shoulder height.
Lower slowly to full extension.
formCues: Keep the elbows pinned to the ribs
commonMistakes: Swinging the torso
Cutting the bottom range short

items.name: Cable triceps pushdown
items.description: Isolates the triceps with constant tension and a very low technique barrier.
instructions: Set a bar or rope at upper-chest height.
Press down until the arms are fully extended.
Return under control to about 90 degrees.
formCues: Elbows stay fixed at the sides
commonMistakes: Leaning over the bar to add bodyweight

items.name: EZ-bar skull crusher
items.description: Loads the triceps in a stretched position, which pushdowns do not reach.
instructions: Lie on a bench holding an EZ bar over the chest.
Bend the elbows to lower the bar toward the forehead.
Extend back to the start without moving the upper arms.
formCues: Upper arms stay still; only the forearms move
commonMistakes: Turning it into a press
Flaring the elbows wide
safetyNotes: Use a controlled tempo; this loads the elbow joint directly

items.name: Barbell shrug
items.description: Direct upper-trap work, useful for posture and for carrying heavy loads.
instructions: Hold a barbell at arm's length in front of the thighs.
Shrug the shoulders straight up toward the ears.
Lower under control to a full stretch.
formCues: Straight up and down, no rolling
commonMistakes: Rolling the shoulders
Bending the elbows to help

items.name: Standing calf raise
items.description: Trains the gastrocnemius through a full range, important for running and jumping.
instructions: Stand with the balls of the feet on a step, heels hanging.
Rise as high as possible onto the toes.
Lower slowly to a deep stretch.
formCues: Pause at the top and at the stretch
commonMistakes: Bouncing through a short range

items.name: Machine leg extension
items.description: Isolates the quads, useful for adding volume without loading the spine.
instructions: Sit with the pad on the lower shins and the knees at the pivot.
Extend the knees to full lockout.
Lower under control.
formCues: Pause briefly at full extension
commonMistakes: Swinging the weight up with momentum

items.name: Hip abduction machine
items.description: Targets the glute medius and abductors, which most compound work under-trains.
instructions: Sit with the pads against the outside of the knees.
Push the knees apart against resistance.
Return under control.
formCues: Lean forward slightly to bias the glutes
commonMistakes: Slamming the pads back together

items.name: Easy run
items.description: Conversational-pace running, the aerobic base of most conditioning programmes.
instructions: Start with five minutes of easy walking or jogging.
Settle into a pace where you can still hold a conversation.
Finish with a few minutes of walking.
formCues: Land under the hips, not out in front
Relax the shoulders and hands
commonMistakes: Running easy days too hard
Increasing weekly volume too quickly
safetyNotes: Increase weekly mileage gradually to protect the shins and knees

items.name: Treadmill run
items.description: Controlled-pace running indoors, useful for precise interval and tempo work.
instructions: Warm up walking for three to five minutes.
Build to the target pace and hold it for the prescribed time.
Cool down at an easy walk.
formCues: Keep a slight incline to better match outdoor effort
commonMistakes: Holding the handrails
Running at zero incline exclusively
safetyNotes: Clip the safety key to your clothing

items.name: Rowing machine
items.description: Full-body, low-impact conditioning that loads the posterior chain as well as the lungs.
instructions: Drive with the legs first, then swing the torso back, then pull the arms.
Reverse the order on the recovery: arms, torso, legs.
Keep a steady stroke rate.
formCues: Legs, body, arms out; arms, body, legs back
commonMistakes: Pulling with the arms first
Rounding the lower back at the catch

items.name: Stationary bike
items.description: Low-impact cardio that spares the joints, ideal for recovery days or high volume.
instructions: Set the saddle so the knee is slightly bent at the bottom of the stroke.
Ride at the prescribed resistance and cadence.
Spin easy to finish.
formCues: Keep the cadence smooth rather than grinding
commonMistakes: Saddle set too low, straining the knees

items.name: Elliptical trainer
items.description: Very low-impact steady-state cardio, useful when running is not tolerated.
instructions: Step on and begin a smooth stride.
Hold the moving handles and keep an upright posture.
Maintain effort for the prescribed duration.
formCues: Stand tall rather than leaning on the console
commonMistakes: Leaning heavily on the fixed rails

items.name: Jump rope
items.description: Extremely high calorie cost per minute plus calf and coordination work in a tiny footprint.
instructions: Hold the handles at hip height with the elbows close in.
Turn the rope with the wrists and make small, quick hops.
Land softly on the balls of the feet.
formCues: Wrists turn the rope, not the arms
Jump just high enough to clear
commonMistakes: Jumping far too high
Swinging from the shoulders
safetyNotes: High calf and Achilles load; build volume gradually

items.name: Battle ropes
items.description: Upper-body dominant conditioning with almost no eccentric load, easy on recovery.
instructions: Hold one rope end in each hand in an athletic stance.
Drive alternating waves down the rope.
Keep the hips loaded and the trunk braced.
formCues: Stay low and let the hips absorb the effort
commonMistakes: Standing upright and using only the arms

items.name: Burpee
items.description: A full-body conditioning staple requiring no equipment and driving heart rate up fast.
instructions: Drop to a squat and place the hands on the floor.
Jump the feet back to a plank and perform a push-up.
Jump the feet in and stand or jump at the top.
formCues: Keep the trunk braced when the feet land in the plank
commonMistakes: Hips sagging in the plank
Letting form collapse as fatigue builds

items.name: Box jump
items.description: Trains explosive hip extension with a soft landing, the entry point to plyometrics.
instructions: Stand a short step from a stable box.
Dip and swing the arms, then jump and land softly on top.
Step down, do not jump down.
formCues: Land quietly with the hips back
Step down every rep
commonMistakes: Jumping down and pounding the joints
Choosing a box too tall to land upright on
safetyNotes: Use a box that will not slide or tip
Always step down between reps

items.name: Single-leg balance
items.description: Builds ankle and hip stability, valuable in warm-ups and in return-from-injury work.
instructions: Stand on one leg with a soft knee.
Hold steady, keeping the hips level.
Progress by closing the eyes or adding reaches.
formCues: Grip the floor gently with the toes
commonMistakes: Letting the hip of the free leg drop

items.name: Leg swings
items.description: A dynamic warm-up drill that opens the hips before squatting, hinging or running.
instructions: Hold a support and swing one leg forward and back.
Keep the trunk still and let the hip do the work.
Repeat side to side, then switch legs.
formCues: Build range gradually rather than forcing it
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back to swing higher

items.name: World's greatest stretch
items.description: A single drill covering hip flexors, hamstrings and thoracic rotation, ideal before training.
instructions: Step into a deep lunge with both hands inside the front foot.
Drop the back hip toward the floor, then rotate the inside arm to the ceiling.
Straighten the front leg to stretch the hamstring, then switch sides.
formCues: Move slowly and breathe into each position
commonMistakes: Rushing through without reaching end range

items.name: Cat-cow
items.description: Gentle segmental spine mobility, useful before lifting or as part of a cool-down.
instructions: Start on hands and knees with a neutral spine.
Exhale and round the back toward the ceiling.
Inhale and arch, lifting the chest and tailbone.
formCues: Move one vertebra at a time
commonMistakes: Moving only at the lower back

items.name: Thoracic rotation
items.description: Restores upper-back rotation, which improves overhead pressing and squat bar position.
instructions: Kneel with one hand behind the head and the elbow tucked.
Rotate the elbow up and open toward the ceiling.
Return and repeat, then switch sides.
formCues: Rotate through the ribcage, keep the hips still
commonMistakes: Twisting from the lower back instead

items.name: Band shoulder dislocate
items.description: Opens the shoulders through a full overhead arc; standard preparation for pressing.
instructions: Hold a band wide in front of the thighs with straight arms.
Raise it overhead and behind the body, keeping the arms straight.
Reverse the path under control.
formCues: Start wider than feels necessary and narrow over time
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows to force the range
safetyNotes: Never force past a painful range

items.name: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch
items.description: Targets hip flexors shortened by prolonged sitting, improving hip extension for hinging.
instructions: Kneel on one knee with the other foot flat in front.
Tuck the pelvis under and squeeze the rear glute.
Shift forward gently and hold, then switch sides.
formCues: The stretch comes from the pelvic tuck, not leaning forward
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back and feeling nothing

items.name: Seated hamstring stretch
items.description: Lengthens the hamstrings after lower-body work; a cool-down staple.
instructions: Sit with one leg extended and the other tucked in.
Hinge forward from the hips over the straight leg.
Hold, breathing steadily, then switch sides.
formCues: Lead with the chest, not the head
commonMistakes: Rounding the back to reach further

items.name: Foam roll quads
items.description: Self-massage of the quads after training; helps perceived recovery and tissue tolerance.
instructions: Lie face down with the roller under the thighs.
Roll slowly from above the knee to the hip.
Pause and breathe on tender spots.
formCues: Move slowly; speed defeats the purpose
commonMistakes: Rolling directly over the kneecap
safetyNotes: Avoid rolling directly over joints or bone
